Name: Pua Kumbu (Iban Ceremonial Textile)
Storytelling: Sacred woven textile of the Iban people. Designs are often received through dreams (mimpi). Traditionally used in rituals; now used for weddings, festivals, and wall art.

Name: Sape (Orang Ulu Boat Lute)
Storytelling: Traditional boat lute of the Orang Ulu (Kayan/Kenyah). Carved from a single wood block. Originally for healing rituals, now the iconic 'sound of Sarawak'.

Name: Keringkam (Sarawak Malay Gold Embroidery)
Storytelling: The 'Crown of Sarawak Malay Women'. A luxury veil embroidered with gold/silver flat threads. Symbol of status, worn at weddings and special functions.

Name: Terendak (Melanau Sun Hat)
Storytelling: Conical hat of the Melanau people, weaved from bamboo and nipah leaves. Features red and black bamboo patterns. Used for protection against sun and rain.

Name: Manik Sarawak (Orang Ulu Beadwork)
Storytelling: Beads (Manik) are heirloom currency for Orang Ulu tribes. Modern artisans create jewelry with traditional motifs like dragons or hornbills.

Name: Tikar Bemban (Bemban Mat)
Storytelling: Woven from the skin of the Bemban plant. Cool to touch and shiny. Essential in Iban longhouses. Patterns often represent rivers or hills.

Name: Bakul Penan (Penan Baskets)
Storytelling: Handwoven baskets by Penan master weavers. Often made from durable PVC straps today. Known as 'to-go' bags for their strength and vibrant colors.

Name: Sarawak Songket
Storytelling: Distinct for 'Songket Tabur' technique and hidden threads. Gold/silver threads woven into silk/cotton. Used for Sampin (men's waist cloth).
